title: Securing Temporary / Scratch Directories in Agentic Python Stacks
content: Insecure temporary file creation is classified under CWE-377 (insecure temp file) and CWE-379 (temp file in directory with insecure permissions); the root attacks are TOCTOU races, symlink hijacking, and predictable path guessing — all three are eliminated by Python's tempfile.mkdtemp() and TemporaryDirectory(), which create directories atomically with mode 0700 (owner-only rwx) and no race window. In agentic stacks the threat surface widens: multiple subagents sharing a world-writable scratch directory enable cross-agent file tampering and, critically, file-based indirect prompt injection — an adversary (or a compromised upstream agent) plants malicious instructions in a tool-output file that a downstream agent later reads and executes, classified as OWASP LLM Top-10 LLM01:2025. CERT FIO21-C codifies the foundational rule: never create temp files in shared world-writable directories; instead, each agent session must own a private, scoped directory unreachable by siblings. Secrets written to temp must be treated as permanently compromised if they ever land in a shared or world-readable path — per NVIDIA's agentic sandboxing guidance, sandbox environments accumulate sensitive artifacts and must be destroyed, not merely cleaned, at session end. The Article-0 rule for ark extends this principle to its strongest form: dot-local private data must never be routed through shared /tmp or any path accessible outside the owning process, and every outbound artifact must pass through the publish guard before leaving the session boundary.
lesson: Ark's session scratchpad already exists; the gap is hardening it: every agent and subagent must receive its own mkdtemp(0700) subdirectory rather than writing into a shared parent, so a compromised or hallucinating subagent cannot plant injection payloads readable by siblings. The Article-0 eternity clause maps directly onto the strongest temp-security rule — dot-local material must never transit through any path (including shared /tmp) that is not owned exclusively by the running process, and teardown must be guaranteed via a context manager even on crash so no sensitive artifact survives the session boundary.
key_usages: instantiate a per-agent secure scratch directory inside ark's session scratchpad with guaranteed 0700 permissions and crash-safe cleanup
refuse to open any file inside the scratch area that resolves through a symlink, blocking cross-agent symlink-hijack and injection attacks
ensure dot-local data never routes through shared /tmp — enforce via the publish guard and by always specifying dir= to a session-owned parent
bound scratch disk usage and destroy the directory tree (not just empty it) at session end to prevent leftover artifact leakage
treat every file read from the scratch area as untrusted external input before including its content in an agent prompt

key_codes.label: secure per-agent mkdtemp context manager (0700, crash-safe cleanup)
key_codes.code:
import os, tempfile, shutil
from contextlib import contextmanager

@contextmanager
def agent_scratchdir(session_root: str, agent_id: str):
    """Atomic 0700 sub-dir scoped to one agent; guaranteed teardown on crash."""
    base = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=f"{agent_id}_", dir=session_root)
    os.chmod(base, 0o700)  # mkdtemp already does 0700; explicit for auditability
    try:
        yield base
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(base, ignore_errors=False)

key_codes.label: symlink-refusing file open inside scratch area (O_NOFOLLOW)
session-root creation: never pass dir=None (falls back to bare /tmp)
key_codes.code:
import os, tempfile

def make_session_root(base_dir: str) -> str:
    """Create 0700 session scratch root. Agents receive mkdtemp subdirs here.
    Always pass explicit dir= so the parent is never bare /tmp.
    """
    os.makedirs(base_dir, mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
    return tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="session_", dir=base_dir)

key_codes.label: Article-0 guard: block dot-local paths from entering scratch writes
